data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"21 pencils cost $6, justified by a causal pricing mechanism where the quoted '7 for $2' establishes a fixed unit-rate of $2/7 per pencil, and the total cost scales deterministically with the quantity purchased.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The store applies a strict bundle-only pricing model where single pencils or non-multiples of 7 cannot be prorated, though for 21 pencils this still yields $6 via 3 bundles.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The store imposes a bulk discount or surcharge for purchasing 21 pencils at once, changing the marginal unit price away from $2/7.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The '7 for $2' is a limited-time promotion or restricted to one per customer, invalidating the assumption that the rate applies uniformly to a 21-pencil purchase.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The store has a tiered pricing structure where the rate for the first 7 pencils differs from the rate for additional pencils beyond the first bundle.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The price quote '7 for $2' causally sets a constant unit price p = $2/7 per pencil via domain-specific uniform pricing conventions. When a customer purchases N=21 pencils, the total cost C is determined by the deterministic multiplicative relation C = N * p = 21 * ($2/7) = $6. The causal link is the application of the uniform rate to the target quantity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
